==English==

===Alternative forms===
* {{alt|en|course||colloquial|ellipsis}}
* {{alt|en|'course||hypercorrect|colloquial|ellipsis}}
* {{alt|en|ofc|oc||Internet slang}}
* {{alt|en|ofcourse||nonstandard|proscribed}}

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/əv ˈkɔːs/|a=RP}}
* {{IPA|en|/əv ˈkɔɹs/|a=GA}}
* {{IPA|en|/əv ˈkoə(ɹ)s/|a=non-horse-hoarse}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-of course.ogg|a=Mid-Atlantic US}}
* {{audio|en|en-au-of course.ogg|a=AU}}

===Adjective===
{{en-adj|?}}

# {{lb|en|now|rare|_|except in ''[[matter of course]]''}} That is part of ordinary behaviour or custom; [[customary]], [[natural]]. {{defdate|from 16th c.}}
#* {{RQ:Landon Francesca Carrara|page=147|volume=III|text=Had Francesca grown up by his side, she would have loved him; and a thousand indulgences, the result of careless good-nature, would have linked the child to the parent, till the mutual affection would have become a thing '''of course'''.}}
#* {{RQ:Macaulay Miscellaneous Writings|chapter=CG Speech 21 March 1849|page=749|passage=I am not using a mere phrase '''of course''', when I say that the feelings with which I bear a part in the ceremony of this day are such as I find it difficult to utter in words.}}

====Derived terms====
{{col|en|matter of course}}

===Adverb===
{{en-adv|-}}

# {{lb|en|now|rare}} {{U|in due course}}; as a [[matter of course]]; as a natural result. {{defdate|from 16th c.}}
#* {{RQ:Smollett Peregrine Pickle|year=1781|chapter=He Is Concerned in a Dangerous Adventure with a Certain Gardener;{{nb...|Sublimes His Ideas, Commences Gallant, and Becomes Acquainted with Miss Emily Gauntlet.}}|page=50|column=2|text=He inſpired love and emulation wherever he appeared; envy and jealous rage followed '''of courſe'''; ſo that he became a very deſirable, though a very dangerous acquaintance.}}
#* {{RQ:Wollstonecraft Vindication Men|passage=Not tarrying long enough in the brain to be subject to reflection, the next sensations, '''of course''', obliterate them.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1845|author=w:Henry John Stephen|title=New commentaries on the laws of England|passage=It was at one time made a question whether giving the royal assent to a single bill did not '''of course''' put an end to the session.}}
# {{U|naturally}}; as would be expected; for obvious reasons, [[obviously]]. {{defdate|from 19th c.}}
#: {{syn|en|naturally|indisputably}}
#: {{ux|en|'''Of course''' I know that!}}
#: {{ux|en|You will  '''of course'''  surrender all your future rights to the property.}}
#* {{RQ:Chambers Younger Set|chapter=A Novice|page=359|passage=“Heavens!” exclaimed Nina, “the blue-stocking and the fogy!—and yours ''are'' pale blue, Eileen!—you’re about as self-conscious as Drina—slumping there with your hair tumbling ''à la'' Mérode! Oh, it’s very picturesque, '''of course''', but a straight spine and good grooming is better.{{nb...}}”}}
#* {{RQ:Lincoln Pratt's Patients|pages=304–305|pageref=304|passage=We tiptoed into the house, up the stairs and along the hall to the door of the room where the Professor had been spending so much of his time. 'Twas locked, '''of course''', but the Deacon man got a big bunch of keys out of his pocket and commenced to putter with the lock.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2012|author=Christoper Zara|title=Tortured Artists: From Picasso and Monroe to Warhol and Winehouse, the Twisted Secrets of the World's Most Creative Minds|section=part 1, chapter 1, {{gbooks|q=of-course|id=HV4jKhjzMVYC|pg=25}}|passage=There were other flapper-era starlets, '''of course'''—Louise Brooks, Greta Garbo—but they were poseurs by comparison.}}
#* {{RQ:Economist|date=2013-06-22|volume=407|issue=8841|page=76|title=[http://www.economist.com/news/books-and-arts/21579801-making-sense-statistics-riddle-our-days-snakes-and-ladders Snakes and ladders]|passage=Risk is everywhere. From tabloid headlines insisting that coffee causes cancer (yesterday, '''of course''', it cured it) to stern government warnings about alcohol and driving, the world is teeming with goblins. For each one there is a frighteningly precise measurement of just how likely it is to jump from the shadows and get you.}}
